text:
maya: Folks — quick sync: we need to lock PRD acceptance criteria for the evidence packaging part of the KMS/HSM audit story. scope: what we hand to customers vs what we keep internally. thoughts?

alex (security): prefer differentiated outputs: 'customer-evidence' (redacted) and 'full-audit' (internal). customers often ask for exported bundles. :+1:

sam (eng): implementation constraints: full-audit bundles are heavy. need to decide format (NDJSON vs tar.gz) and whether we support per-tenant on-demand export or only scheduled snapshots.

jordan (compliance): SOC2 wants immutable chain of custody metadata, time-synced events, and proof of retention policy application. also need retention deletion logs for evidence that data was expunged.

maya: good notes. two tradeoffs to decide now: 1) export formats & compression, 2) retention tiers (default 90d vs enterprise 7y). also whether export includes raw HSM telemetry.

lee (legal): watch cross-border transfers. if a customer requests an export that includes telemetry, we must ensure PII is scrubbed or consented. include a checkbox in the PRD: exports must include a data classification flag.

sam (eng): proposed minimal RFC config example:```json
{"retention_tiers": [
  {"name": "standard", "days": 90, "encrypt_at_rest": true},
  {"name": "enterprise", "days": 2555, "requires_contract": true}
],
"export_formats": ["ndjson", "tar.gz"],
"include_hsm_telemetry": "opt-in"
}```

alex (security): +1 to opt-in telemetry. Also require signed manifests for each export (SHA256) and an audit manifest that records who downloaded.

jordan (compliance): acceptance criteria checklist draft:
- export package includes manifest with SHA256 hashes
- timestamps normalized to UTC with millisecond precision
- redaction policy applied per data-class flag
- proof of deletion retained for 30d after deletion action
- ability to produce chain-of-custody for any export request within 48 hours

maya: can we make the "proof of deletion" a tamper-evident record? maybe a signed event by KMS-key used for rotation?

alex (security): yes — sign deletion event with current KMS key and include key fingerprint. store signatures in HSM-backed ledger. note: that introduces key rotation edge cases we must enumerate in RFC.

sam (eng): edge cases to put in RFC: partial deletes (customer deletes subset of keys), archival vs active, export during rolling key rotation, and very-large exports (>100GB) — must trigger async URL + chunking.

lee (legal): include DSAR handling: if DSAR requires erasure, exports must exclude erased records and we need attestations for removed entries. also clause about law enforcement holds.

maya: action items for PRD/RFC:
- sam: draft export/format RFC with async download flow + chunking (due EOD Tue)
- alex: spec signed-manifest + deletion-signature flow + key-rotation edge cases (due Wed)
- jordan: map SOC2 acceptance language to checklist items above and confirm retention floor (due Wed)
- lee: legal wording for cross-border & DSARs to include in PRD (due Fri)
- ops-bot: create RFC ticket and link requirements (ops-bot: RFC #3582 created -> https://rfc.internal/3582)

ops-bot: RFC #3582 created and assigned to sam, alex, jordan, lee. Due dates set on tickets.

maya: final ask — include a short 'customer experience' blurb in PRD: how a customer requests exports, expected SLA (48h for ready-to-download <50GB, longer for >50GB), and cost disclosures. we need this before we present to sales. :thinking:

alex (security): ok. I’ll also add a short note about vulnerability exposure if exports include telemetry.

sam (eng): will mock the download flow and link to a small HAR of the async flow in the RFC.

maya: great. I'll consolidate acceptance criteria into the PRD after we get the RFC drafts. Thanks everyone — we're aiming to gate launch on these items being in place. :rocket:
